title: The Ley Hunter
subtitle: On sleepless nights, she counts the stars alone.

items.text: Children's Square, Rayashki
A lonely researcher aimlessly paces through Rayashki's square.
The town's cold wind clearly cannot smooth the wrinkles of her brow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Could I really have traded the future of these people away for my ley line studies?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: *sighs* Zeno ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I was a mule chasing after a carrot on a stick. They lured me here all so I could help ruin everything!
Her voice bursts up from her chest.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Heh! You seem to be in a good mood.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We taught Zeno a lesson. They were forced to leave with their devil's bargains and tails tucked behind them. We fought back, finally.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: A nice little trick, that was. Thank you, Comrade Windsong.
She smiles at Windsong, giving her a wink.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We all know who the mysterious hero was that gave us a helping hand.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I, I didn't do anything.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It's no shame to have helped your friends, not to mention to stand up to Zeno.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Have more confidence in yourself, Comrade Windsong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But will you really gain anything from this fight?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Not sure, but we have to do something, right?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's why I'm here.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: To talk to me?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I don't know why, but Ms. Vila, you must have thought too much of me.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: In fact, I'm only a simple researcher. I'm not powerful enough to change Zeno's decision.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You are the one thinking too much, Comrade Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Your ley line lessons were much more popular than you think. They have had a positive effect on the children.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Now, they are looking at the bigger picture and observing the world in a more detailed way. You've unleashed their curiosity.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Is the aurora the bubbles spit out by the stars? They form such a beautiful map. Do they study ley lines, too?"
Vila feigns distress, shaking her head with a pretended childlike confusion.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But it remains the case that the study of ley lines has never been verified.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: For all its ambitions. Only a limited number of people studied it in the past decades, and that number is decreasing even now.
Vila nods thoughtfully.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What you are looking at is not some skin problem, but my past.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: My past as a Rusalka.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Rusalka? You mean the mermaid from folklore?!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: My people used to live in a far-secluded place in the north, away from the humans.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: For hundreds of years, there was only hostility, plunder, and slaughter between us and them.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We only started to learn more about each other in the last few decades, and then I was born. It's been a hard life growing up within human society, but I've become used to it.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Still, some things never got easier.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Most humans still thought I was a freak. They "welcomed" me with mocking, sarcasm, and contempt for my people, my heritage.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: As for the Rusalki, they too found a half-blooded mermaid unacceptable. They didn't approve of my living among the humans, forcing me to live as a fugitive in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
"Half-blooded." It was a nauseating term, one separating the Rusalki from the "scaleless" humans who had stolen their homeland.
An ancient myth that was the source of the enduring hatred between Rusalki and humans.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They tried to catch me by every means possible, so they could wash away the "stain" they saw in me.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: That sounds very difficult.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Humans have stigmatized and hunted the Rusalki for centuries, while Rusalki still have the instinct to attack and plunder human ships even now.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: How are they supposed to make peace in such little time?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That was what I thought years ago. Then, I came to this town.
She surveys the white land; the unifying cover of snow removes all distinctions, differences, and flaws.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "A wonderful world where humans and Rusalki could live in peace." I was finally convinced.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: In Rayashki, everyone can make contributions with their skills, whether you are a human, a Rusalka, or a ley line researcher.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I don't mean to give you more stress or push you. You will always be our friend, whatever your choice is.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But this is not an unreachable dream. It's real.
A familiar phrase wells up inside her again.
Conjured from a long-silenced past.
School of Ley Lines

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Haha!
The girl, then much thinner and more stubborn than now, couldn't help but cheer.
The other ley hunters fail to take notice, as they comb through their scattered papers.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The editor of the Environmental Research agreed to publish our report, finally!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But he only gave us 5000 words.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: On the last few pages.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Undoubtedly, it's still a good start, our first step to reviving the study of ley lines!
Windsong beams with excitement, clumsily sprawling over the table to select from their papers with care.
Dull, dry theories shine anew, bright and vivid in her eyes.
A table of twinkling stars.
Yet, these stars must shine against an all-consuming field of darkness.

items.speaker: Ley Hunter I
items.text: That's it. I give up! Maybe I'll study something else, like urban planning, or landscape design.

items.speaker: Ley Hunter I
items.text: At least I can make a living that way.
Windsong remains buried in her heap of books and manuscripts, oblivious to the loss.

items.speaker: Ley Hunter II
items.text: The study of ley lines is outdated. Everyone agrees now that it can't be verified by science.

items.speaker: Ley Hunter II
items.text: "This whole study was a dead end. Ley lines are only a baseless theory of arcanum."
The old papers on the table filled with nothing more than nonsense and wasted ink.
At least that's how the world received it.

items.speaker: Ley Hunter III
items.text: I tried talking about our study of ley lines with other arcanists, but almost no one has ever heard of it. They are more interested in Laplace's breakthroughs.

items.speaker: Ley Hunter III
items.text: Or anecdotes in their own fields, like the Chaotic Energy sampling mentioned in the paper written by the Butterfly of Lorentz.
The stars have dimmed.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So, maybe it is an unreachable dream?
A long moment of wistful distraction falls back into reality.
After much hesitation, she begins to speak again.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I do wish I could help, but ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It would take a lot of resources to verify the theory behind ley lines. There may be even danger and sacrifice.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Even Zeno has paid little attention to my research. They only see it as a means to an end.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Researchers in other fields can stand on the shoulders of giants, while I, I don't even have a school to return to.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I doubt that the study of ley lines will help you much.
She retreats a few steps back.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Well, thank you for your honesty, Comrade Windsong.
Vila looks away, holding the regret deep in her chest.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'll see you soon.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: See you, Vila.
She bows her head and turns, taking a few more difficult steps away.
Perhaps it was her unattainable dream of revival that slowed her, or the weight of all that had gone wrong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Wait, Comrade Windsong!
A burst of light steps leaps toward her once more.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Don't forget your next lesson. The children are still waiting.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But the town is ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Life must continue, comrade.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We can't let our worries stop us.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Okay.
